question: What rules and numbers do the soldier traversal graphs (in air, sliding, support, vault, swimming, parachute, ladder, zipline) hold?

sourceFacts.method: Compiled expression graphs were listed with expression-graphs/exgraph.py (format from L4016, names from L4017 and L4019) and read section by section by a delegated reader; each constant cited here was then checked at its raw offset in the resource file. Full reading: expression-graphs/findings/traversal.md.

control.description: Every cited constant is a raw-offset check against the resource body. Function meanings marked inferred in the findings file are not relied on for the checked values.

points: `SimEx_InAirExpressions`: landing class by vertical speed vy: above -6.2 class 0, above -13 class 1, above -15.7 class 2, above -18.45 class 3, above -21.23 class 4, above -29.5 class 5, otherwise 7; class 6 for a jump landing above -13. A second copy fires only when close to ground with vy below -2. No damage is applied in this graph.

`SimEx_SlidingLogic`: factor = (clamp(`TimeSinceLastDiveOrSlide`, 1.25, 2.5) - 1.25) / 2.5 + 0.5; slide limit = clamp(factor x `Slide.ImpulseLength` x curve(speed) / 6.5, 0, 1); slide speed clamped to 5..100.
`SimEx_CheckSupport`: OnGround when ground distance < 0.1, CloseToGround when < 0.3, and a next-frame prediction using distance + vy x frame time.
Swimming vault (`SimEx_CheckStartVault_Swimming`): window from 1.25 up to `Vault_Swimming_StartHeightMax`, with constants 0.5, 0.4 and 0.2.

In-air vault runs only for non-AI soldiers holding the vault input. Parachute steering is slew-limited at 0.8 per second with drag capped at 50; ladder entry has a 75 degree facing cone; zipline and rope detach on jump, crouch, vehicle entry or abort. These rows are a delegated reading and not individually raw-checked.

inference: The landing classes probably select landing animation and fall-damage tier; the damage per tier is not in these graphs.
`7bec9f8f` reads as subtract and `e6117a11` as less-than from consistent use across graphs.
With gravity 9.81, -6.2 m/s is a drop of about 2 m and -13 m/s about 8.6 m; that conversion is arithmetic, not read.
unresolved: Tunable values (impulse length, swim speeds, zipline speeds, vault maxima) are named here but stored elsewhere.
One branch in the landing-class code has an unprinted jump, so class 0 for vy above -6.2 is read from structure.
Unnamed curve imports are not resolved.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Traversal graphs read: landing class is picked by vertical speed at -6.2, -13, -15.7, -18.45, -21.23 and -29.5 m/s, slide strength scales from 0.5 at 1.25 s to 1.0 at 2.5 s since the last slide or dive, and on-ground and close-to-ground are distances under 0.1 and 0.3
leads.summary: The traversal graphs were read. Landing class 0 to 7 is chosen by vertical speed bands at -6.2, -13, -15.7, -18.45, -21.23 and -29.5; the graph applies no fall damage itself. Slide strength = (clamp(time since last slide or dive, 1.25, 2.5) - 1.25) / 2.5 + 0.5, so 0.5 right after a slide and 1.0 from 2.5 s; slide speed is clamped to 5..100. On ground is a ground distance under 0.1, close to ground under 0.3. 16 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: The fall-damage data is joined to the landing classes, or the slide tunables are joined.
leads.statusNote: Landing bands, slide scaling and support thresholds read; constants raw-checked.
